summary: A lookout tower at the MacClenny forestry station in Baker County, listed in a 1957 report; its builder is unconfirmed.

access.note: Sits at a forestry station. The register does not describe public access; ask before visiting.

events.note: Listed among the MacClenny headquarters buildings in a January 1957 newspaper report
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, June 6, 2026

corrections.why: The register names the Florida Forest Service as administrator, and the 1957 report says the state built the station's buildings. These sources show state administration and construction, not land title, so verify before applying.
The register spells the site out as the MacClenny Forestry Station; the record's abbreviated bracketed form is a parsing artifact.

evidence.supports: location on U.S. 90 west of Glen St Mary at the MacClenny forestry station
evidence.quote: Located at the MacClenny forestry station on U.S. 90, west of Glen St Mary.

evidence.supports: nominator's guess that it was a WPA project
evidence.quote: I believe it was a WPA project.

evidence.supports: tower stood on a turpentine camp no longer open
evidence.quote: It was on a turpentine camp that is no longer open.

evidence.supports: administered by the Florida Forest Service
site is the MacClenny Forestry Station
January 1957 report; headquarters 1.5 miles west of Glen St. Mary on US 90 with office, lookout tower, garage and warehouse
evidence.quote: consists of an office building, lookout tower, garage and warehouse

evidence.supports: buildings constructed and equipment furnished by the state after a referendum
evidence.quote: The buildings were constructed and equipment furnished by the state after Baker County voters expressed their approval in a referendum.

evidence.supports: county share of operating cost through a two-mill levy
evidence.quote: a special two mill tax levy

notes_for_editor: Only two thin sources, and the build date and builder are unknown. The register's WPA claim is the nominator's own belief ('I believe'). A Florida Memory catalogue entry titled 'Gate entrance and tower at CCC camp in Pine Top' (floridamemory.com/items/show/62708) appeared in search results and points the other way, but floridamemory.com returned HTTP 403 to fetch_text, so it is not cited; check it by hand. The 1957 article's state-built line covers the headquarters buildings and does not say whether the tower was one of them. Access is marked restricted only because the tower sits at a forestry station. Note for the team: the 'A Legacy Remembered' CCC marker (hmdb.org m=55674) surfaced in a Pine Top search, but its coordinates and text place it at Olustee, not Pine Top, so it is not used here. The record's ownership 'federal' is the main correction proposed; the agency field already reads Florida Forest Service.
